fleets.attentionNote: Axon body-worn, in-car (Fleet), dock, or TASER gear. IEEE OUI 00:25:DF is Axon Enterprise. Body 3/4 often advertise BLE on that public OUI while worn. A name like Axon Body is a pattern, not that officer. Quiet or LTE-only units will not appear. The word Axon also hits some ZTE phones. Look with your eyes. Not identity.

fleets.name: BlipTrack
fleets.notes: BLIP Systems BlipTrack roadside Bluetooth/Wi-Fi travel-time sensor. Same job as BlueTOAD Spectra: samples passing phones and in-car radios at two points for speed. Quiet or Ethernet-only cabinets may not advertise. Pattern match, not that cabinet.

fleets.name: Blue Maestro

fleets.name: BlueTOAD Spectra
fleets.notes: Iteris roadside Bluetooth travel-time reader (Vantage Velocity, now BlueTOAD Spectra / Spectra CV). Samples phones, headsets, and in-car Bluetooth as vehicles pass; matching the same ID at two points gives speed. About 100 m. A sample, not a full count. Quiet or Ethernet-only cabinets may not advertise. Spectra CV also uses 5.9 GHz C-V2X, which Fieldwatch cannot hear. IEEE Iteris OUI can also hit other Iteris roadside kit. Pattern match, not that cabinet.

fleets.name: BMW
fleets.notes: BMW phone-as-key or in-car hotspot. Factory BMW_ Wi-Fi is the car, not a dealer showroom.

fleets.name: Bose
fleets.notes: Bose headphones or speaker. Quiet Charge / QC buds advertise even when in the case.

fleets.name: Brilliant Frame

fleets.name: Bruce

fleets.name: DULT tracker

enumNotes.0: Separated from its owner. The address can hold still for about a day.
enumNotes.1: Near its owner. With you the whole sit, this is often your own tag. First heard after the sit started, it is more often someone who joined with their own keys.

fleets.name: DWnet
fleets.notes: DWnet consumer / SMB access point. Cloud SSIDs are house names, so the board vendor is the hit.

fleets.name: Fitbit
fleets.notes: Fitbit watch or tracker. Advertisements are identity-only; step counts are not in the broadcast.

fleets.name: Flock Safety Cameras

fleets.attentionNote: Flock-style roadside ALPR / camera pole — reads plates and can be used to locate a vehicle. IEEE B4:1E:52 or a Flock-* SSID is the strong hit. Current poles are often quiet on Wi-Fi and BLE. Pattern match, not that camera. Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: FOBO TPMS

fleets.name: Ford

fleets.name: Friend Pendant
fleets.notes: Friend AI necklace — wearable companion that listens.
fleets.attentionNote: Friend Pendant / necklace. BLE service 1a3fd0e7. It listens to conversations. Not proof someone is recording you. A miss is not a clean bill (off, or a different brand). Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: FS Ext Battery
fleets.notes: External battery pack usually associated with a Flock-style camera pole. Name hits are stronger. Current poles are often quiet on Wi-Fi and BLE.
fleets.attentionNote: Usually associated with a Flock-style camera — an external battery pack on the pole. Name hits are stronger. Current poles are often quiet on Wi-Fi and BLE. Pattern match, not that camera. Look with your eyes.

enumNotes.65: Separated from its owner. The address can hold still for about a day.
enumNotes.64: Nearby its owner. With you the whole sit, this is often your own tag. First heard after the sit started, it is more often someone who joined with their own keys.

fleets.name: Helium

fleets.name: Hobby BLE serial
fleets.notes: Cheap hobby UART module advertised under a default name (HM-10, JDY, CC41, ESP32 BLE). Common on printers, cars, and DIY. Fieldwatch does not see Classic HC-05/HC-06.
fleets.attentionNote: These default BLE serial names are cheap hobby modules. Some pump/ATM overlays have used boards like this so someone nearby can pull data over Bluetooth. The same modules show up on printers, cars, and DIY. If this radio is loud next to a card reader, treat it with caution and look with your eyes. Not proof of a skimmer. A miss is not a clean bill (name changed, Classic HC-05/HC-06, or cellular). Fieldwatch does not connect and does not try default PINs. Fieldwatch does not see Classic HC-05/HC-06.

fleets.name: Honda

fleets.name: Novatel Wireless
fleets.notes: Novatel Wireless / Inseego vehicle radio. The same prefix is also on some consumer MiFi hotspots.
fleets.attentionNote: Novatel Wireless / Inseego OUI 28:80:A2. Reported in public-safety vehicle AP work. Same prefix is also on some Inseego consumer MiFi radios. Pattern match, not that agency. Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: Nuki
fleets.notes: Nuki smart lock or opener (retrofit on a European cylinder).

fleets.name: Omi
fleets.notes: Omi / OpenGlass wearable recorder or camera glasses. Arduino-default 19B10000 is too common to use as a rule.
fleets.attentionNote: Omi pendant or OpenGlass camera glasses. Name or BLE service 23ba7924. It can record audio (OpenGlass also has a camera). Not proof someone is recording you. A miss is not a clean bill (off, renamed, or a DIY board using other names). Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: Omron
fleets.notes: Omron blood-pressure cuff or body-composition scale. Home / clinic health kit, not industrial Omron.

fleets.name: OpenWrt
fleets.notes: OpenWrt factory SSID on a flashed travel / DIY router that was never renamed.

fleets.name: Orbit B-hyve
fleets.notes: Orbit B-hyve hose timer / irrigation.

fleets.name: Osmo
fleets.notes: DJI Osmo handheld / action camera (Action, Pocket, 360, Nano). Not a flying DJI aircraft.

fleets.name: Oura
fleets.notes: Oura wellness ring. Always-on BLE while worn. Pattern match, not that person.

fleets.name: Smartwatch
fleets.notes: Smartwatch advertising its product name. Pattern match, not that person.

fleets.name: Pacific TPMS
fleets.notes: Pacific Industrial OEM tire electronics. BLE TPMS on some newer vehicles.

fleets.name: Panasonic i-PRO
fleets.notes: Panasonic i-PRO camera or Arbitrator in-car system. Panasonic TVs and phones use other names.
fleets.attentionNote: Panasonic i-PRO camera or Arbitrator in-car video. Used on buildings and some patrol cars — video and sometimes plates. Name-only (i-PRO / Arbitrator). Not every Panasonic radio. Pattern match, not that camera. Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: Parrot
fleets.notes: Parrot ANAFI, Bebop, or Skycontroller. In-flight digital license plate is the Remote ID row. Not a Parrot car kit.

fleets.name: Paxton
fleets.notes: Paxton / Net2 door reader or access panel.

fleets.name: Pebblebee / moto tag
fleets.notes: Pebblebee or Motorola moto tag item finder. A tag you clip to keys or a bag.

fleets.name: Penguin
fleets.notes: Penguin Flock-family external battery. The XUNTONG BLE manufacturer ID is the usual fingerprint; Penguin* names are older firmware. Newer packs often advertise a 10-digit name. Decode fields show the TN serial from manufacturer data when present.
fleets.attentionNote: Penguin is a Flock-family external battery (XUNTONG manufacturer ID). Name hits are older firmware and low uniqueness. Pattern match, not that camera. Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: PeopleNet
fleets.notes: PeopleNet truck ELD / fleet Wi-Fi. Separate from Motive.

fleets.name: Peplink
fleets.notes: Peplink / Pepwave travel or branch router.

fleets.name: Phone hotspot
fleets.notes: Phone personal hotspot on a factory name (AndroidAP, Galaxy, Pixel). Custom hotspot names miss. iPhone hotspots stay on Apple Device.

fleets.name: Pigvision
fleets.notes: Pigvision Flock-family / roadside camera name.
fleets.attentionNote: Pigvision is a Flock-family / roadside camera name. Name-only. Pattern match, not that camera. Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: Plaud Note
fleets.notes: Plaud Note / NotePin AI meeting recorder.
fleets.attentionNote: Plaud Note / NotePin AI recorder. It records meetings. Not proof someone is recording you. A miss is not a clean bill (off, renamed, or a different brand). Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: Plume
fleets.notes: Plume SuperPod / HomePass mesh. ISP-branded pods (xFi and similar) often use the carrier OEM board instead.

fleets.name: Pokemon GO Plus
fleets.notes: Nintendo Pokémon GO Plus or Plus + wrist accessory. Not a Joy-Con or Switch.

fleets.name: Porkchop
fleets.notes: Porkchop pentest firmware on a Cardputer or Cheap Yellow Display. Default AP name PORKCHOP. BLE spam that spoofs Apple/Android is not this row.
fleets.attentionNote: M5PORKCHOP / Porkchop — pocket Wi-Fi pentest firmware (Cardputer or Cheap Yellow Display). Default CYD remote AP is named PORKCHOP. BACON-mode fake APs brand vendor IE 50:52:4B. A miss is not a clean bill (renamed, passive only, or no AP). Pattern match, not identity, not proof of an attack. Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: Porsche
fleets.notes: Porsche phone-as-key or factory Porsche_WLAN hotspot. Separate from Volkswagen.

fleets.name: Potensic
fleets.notes: Potensic drone, including ATOM. The name starts with Potensic. A bare ATOM name does not match. A renamed network misses. Often no Remote ID plate.

fleets.name: Pwnagotchi
fleets.notes: Pwnagotchi-style Wi-Fi handshake collector. Classic units use a distinctive BSSID and the name pwnagotchi.
fleets.attentionNote: Pwnagotchi-style Wi-Fi handshake collector. Classic units beacon BSSID de:ad:be:ef:de:ad. A pwnagotchi name is a pattern. Not proof of an attack. Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: RadiaCode
fleets.notes: RadiaCode handheld radiation detector.

fleets.name: RAK WisGate
fleets.notes: RAKwireless WisGate LoRaWAN gateway setup AP (RAK7268_XXXX and similar). Quiet once it is on Ethernet.

fleets.name: Raven / ShotSpotter
fleets.notes: Flock Raven or ShotSpotter-style acoustic gunshot sensor, usually on a pole with cameras. BLE UUIDs 3100–3500 are the Raven radio. The XUNTONG battery manufacturer ID is Penguin, not this row. Current Flock-family poles are often quiet on Wi-Fi and BLE.

fleets.name: Ray-Ban / Meta glasses
fleets.notes: Ray-Ban Meta / Oakley Meta smart glasses, or a Quest / other Meta wearable.
fleets.attentionNote: Meta / Luxottica BLE — often Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses. The same company IDs show up on Quest headsets and other Meta wearables. Not proof someone is recording. A miss is not a clean bill (paired and quiet, asleep, or a different brand). Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: RayNeo
fleets.notes: RayNeo smart glasses. Matches only when the name starts with RayNeo and the advertisement uses the TCL company id. A TCL phone without that name does not match.
fleets.attentionNote: RayNeo smart glasses. The name has to start with RayNeo, and the advertisement has to use the TCL company id. A TCL phone without that name does not match. Not proof of recording. A miss is not a clean bill (off, renamed, or paired and quiet). Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: Rekor
fleets.notes: Rekor highway or transit plate reader.
fleets.attentionNote: Rekor is highway / transit ALPR — reads plates on roads and at checkpoints. Name-only. Pattern match, not that camera. Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: Remote ID
fleets.notes: In-flight drone digital license plate (ASTM / FAA Remote ID). Decoded fields can show ID, position, heading, and operator. The French Direct Remote ID vendor IE labels this row too. That plate does not fill position or pilot. Pattern match, not a tail number. Wi-Fi Remote ID often misses on stock Android.

fleets.name: Reolink
fleets.notes: Reolink home / small-business camera. Consumer camera, not a roadside pole.

fleets.name: Retail LED sign
fleets.notes: BLE LED message display. The advertised name is the sign text, not a product name.

fleets.name: Reveal Media
fleets.notes: Reveal Media / BodyWorn camera. Common in UK and some US agencies. Quiet units will not appear.
fleets.attentionNote: Reveal Media body-worn camera (D-series / BodyWorn). Name-only when advertised. Patrol units may stay quiet. Pattern match, not that officer. Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: Rhombus
fleets.notes: Rhombus cloud camera. BLE is loudest when the camera is unregistered or offline.
fleets.attentionNote: Rhombus cloud cameras on buildings and some public sites. IEEE CC:47:BD or a Rhombus name. BLE often only while unregistered or offline. Pattern match, not that camera. Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: Ring
fleets.notes: Amazon Ring doorbell or camera. Common on houses. Consumer camera, not a roadside pole.

fleets.name: Rivian
fleets.notes: Rivian phone-as-key, camp speaker, or sensor. Phones can advertise Rivian Sensor.

fleets.name: Roku
fleets.notes: Roku streaming stick or Roku TV. Often a hidden Wi-Fi Direct AP for the remote. Not an ISP router.

fleets.name: Ruckus
fleets.notes: RUCKUS Unleashed / ZoneFlex campus access point. Not the Arris cable-modem family.

fleets.name: Ruijie
fleets.notes: Ruijie / Reyee campus or SMB access point.

fleets.name: Ruuvi
fleets.notes: Ruuvi broadcast sensor tag (temp / humidity / pressure / motion). Decoded fields on this page parse the sensor payload.

fleets.name: Sagemcom
fleets.notes: Sagemcom ISP gateway. Common Comcast / other cable OEM.

fleets.name: SALTO
fleets.notes: SALTO commercial access lock or reader.

fleets.name: Samsara
fleets.notes: Samsara fleet tracker or vehicle Wi-Fi. Truck / van telematics, adjacent to Motive.

fleets.name: Samsung appliance
fleets.notes: Samsung Family Hub fridge, range, or oven setup Wi-Fi. Not a SmartTag.

fleets.name: Samsung SmartTags
fleets.notes: Samsung SmartTag / SmartTag+ item finder. Addresses often rotate.

fleets.name: Schlage
fleets.notes: Schlage / Allegion smart lock (Encode and similar).

fleets.name: Schrader TPMS
fleets.notes: Schrader aftermarket BLE TPMS (AirCheck, trailer, RV). Not the 315/433 MHz factory stems.

fleets.name: SenseCAP
fleets.notes: Seeed SenseCAP LoRaWAN / Helium indoor gateway setup AP (SenseCAP_XXXXXX). Quiet once it is on Ethernet. Helium-named units can also hit the Helium row.

fleets.name: Sensi
fleets.notes: Sensi thermostat in BLE setup.

fleets.name: SensorPush
fleets.notes: SensorPush temperature / humidity logger.

fleets.name: Sercomm
fleets.notes: Sercomm ISP gateway. Common cable / fiber OEM.

fleets.name: Shokz
fleets.notes: Shokz bone-conduction headphones (OpenRun / OpenFit). Worn on the head, not a tracker.

fleets.name: Skydio
fleets.notes: Skydio drone (common in US public-safety / enterprise). In-flight Remote ID is often Wi-Fi and easy to miss — the Remote ID row is the license plate.

fleets.name: Snap Spectacles
fleets.notes: Snap Spectacles or other Snap BLE product.
fleets.attentionNote: Snapchat BLE company ID — used by Snap Spectacles. Other Snap BLE products could match. Not proof of recording. Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: SnapAV
fleets.notes: Control4 / Wattbox home-AV processor or power unit.

fleets.name: Sonos
fleets.notes: Sonos home/office speaker. Setup or idle ads. Not a tracker.

fleets.name: Sony
fleets.notes: Sony headphones, TV, or camera. Bravia TVs also send a generic iBeacon for Cast — Fieldwatch keeps Sony.

fleets.name: Sophos
fleets.notes: Sophos firewall or access point. Campus / SMB Wi-Fi, not a camera pole.

fleets.name: Spectrum
fleets.notes: Charter Spectrum setup or hotspot Wi-Fi. Boxes are usually Arris / Hitron / Technicolor OEM.

fleets.name: Starlink
fleets.notes: Starlink router. The BSSID is often randomized now — the STARLINK name is the usual hit.

fleets.name: Subaru
fleets.notes: Subaru phone-as-key / infotainment. Not Starlink satellite internet.

fleets.name: SwellPro
fleets.notes: SwellPro waterproof drone. The name starts with SwellPro. A renamed network misses. Often no Remote ID plate.

fleets.name: Synology
fleets.notes: Synology NAS or router access point.

fleets.name: SYTPMS
fleets.notes: SYTPMS / BR bicycle or scooter BLE tire sensor. Decoded fields can show gauge pressure, temperature, battery, and motion. Pattern match, not that vehicle.

fleets.name: T-Mobile
fleets.notes: T-Mobile Home Internet or hotspot. Gateways are often HUMAX / Arcadyan / Askey OEM.

fleets.name: Tapo
fleets.notes: TP-Link Tapo home camera. Consumer camera, not a roadside pole.

fleets.name: Tattile
fleets.notes: Tattile ALPR camera, common on European roads and some US sites.
fleets.attentionNote: Tattile plate readers on roads and at gates. Name-only when advertised. Pattern match, not that camera. Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: Tedee
fleets.notes: Tedee retrofit smart lock.

fleets.name: Tello
fleets.notes: Ryze Tello or Tello Talent. The name starts with TELLO or RMTT. A renamed network misses. Often no Remote ID plate.

fleets.name: Tenda
fleets.notes: Tenda consumer router or extender.

fleets.name: Tesla
fleets.notes: Tesla phone-as-key, vehicle, Wall Connector, or TeslaGW Wi-Fi. iOS also sees an iBeacon layout from the car — that is still Tesla, not a mall beacon. Tire sensors are the tsTPMS row.

fleets.name: Tesla tsTPMS
fleets.notes: Tesla BLE tire sensor. Decoded fields can show pressure, temperature, and battery when the sensor is awake. Pattern match, not that car. Phone-as-key stays on the Tesla row.

fleets.name: Tile Trackers
fleets.notes: Tile item finder. Decoded fields can show a rotating private id — not a serial.

fleets.name: TireCheck
fleets.notes: TireCheck BLE tire-pressure sensor. Pattern match, not that vehicle.

fleets.name: Toyota
fleets.notes: Toyota or Lexus phone-as-key, or a factory TOYOTA / LEXUS hotspot.

fleets.name: TP-Link
fleets.notes: TP-Link or Deco home router / mesh. A Tapo camera on a TP-Link board can also hit this row.

fleets.name: TPMS service
fleets.notes: Bluetooth SIG Tire Pressure Monitoring System service. Any sensor that advertises that standard service.

fleets.name: TRENDnet
fleets.notes: TRENDnet consumer access point.

fleets.name: Tuya
fleets.notes: Tuya plug, light, camera, or sensor. Dense in some apartments. Decoded fields can show whether it is bound.

fleets.name: Uconnect
fleets.notes: Stellantis Uconnect in-car hotspot (Chrysler, Jeep, Ram, Dodge, Fiat). BSSID often randomized.

fleets.name: UniFi
fleets.notes: UniFi / Ubiquiti name on Wi-Fi or BLE. Prefer UniFi AP for BSSID hits. Instant cameras stay on UniFi Protect.

fleets.name: UniFi AP
fleets.notes: UniFi / Ubiquiti Wi-Fi access point (including airMAX / AmpliFi). Renamed SSIDs still hit on the board vendor or Ubiquiti vendor tag. Instant cameras stay on UniFi Protect.

fleets.name: UniFi Protect
fleets.notes: UniFi Protect Instant camera in BLE setup. Not a UniFi Wi-Fi access point.

fleets.name: Uniview
fleets.notes: Uniview / UNV / Uniarch camera. Common on commercial CCTV and some public poles.
fleets.attentionNote: Uniview / UNV cameras. Common on commercial CCTV and some public poles. IEEE Zhejiang Uniview OUIs or a Uniview / UNV- name. Pattern match, not that camera. Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: Utility Inc
fleets.notes: Utility, Inc vehicle or public-safety access point.
fleets.attentionNote: Utility, Inc radio. Reported in public-safety vehicle AP work. Pattern match, not that agency. Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: Vantiva
fleets.notes: Vantiva (ex-Technicolor) ISP gateway. After the ISP renames the Wi-Fi, the board vendor still hits.

fleets.name: Verizon
fleets.notes: Verizon or Fios hotspot / gateway name. Many FiOS boxes are Actiontec OEM.

fleets.name: Verkada
fleets.notes: Verkada cloud camera, including LPR-capable bullets, on buildings and some public sites.
fleets.attentionNote: Verkada cloud cameras, including LPR-capable bullets. Used on buildings and some public sites — video and sometimes plates. Name-only. Pattern match, not that camera. Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: Volkswagen
fleets.notes: Volkswagen phone-as-key or My VW hotspot. Skoda, SEAT, and Porsche have their own rows.

fleets.name: Vuzix
fleets.notes: Vuzix smart glasses or other Vuzix BLE wearable.
fleets.attentionNote: Vuzix BLE glasses. Not proof of recording. A miss is not a clean bill (paired and quiet, asleep, or a different brand). Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: WatchGuard AP
fleets.notes: WatchGuard firewall or access point. Not WatchGuard Video body-worn cameras.

fleets.name: WatchGuard Video
fleets.notes: WatchGuard Video body-worn or in-car camera (now Motorola). Not the WatchGuard firewall company. Patrol units may stay quiet.
fleets.attentionNote: WatchGuard Video body-worn or in-car (VISTA / V300 family). IEEE OUI 00:1D:96 is WatchGuard Video, not the WatchGuard firewall company. Patrol units may stay quiet. Pattern match, not identity. Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: WAVLINK
fleets.notes: WAVLINK consumer travel / home router.

fleets.name: Winegard
fleets.notes: Winegard RV or marine Wi-Fi antenna / router.

fleets.name: Withings
fleets.notes: Withings (Nokia Health) scale or BPM Connect cuff. Not a Nokia phone and not a Nokia ISP gateway.

fleets.name: Wolfcom
fleets.notes: Wolfcom body-worn or in-car camera. Quiet units will not appear.
fleets.attentionNote: Wolfcom body-worn or in-car camera. Name-only when advertised. Patrol units may stay quiet. Pattern match, not that officer. Look with your eyes.

fleets.name: Wyze
fleets.notes: Wyze home camera. Very common consumer gear, not a roadside pole.

fleets.name: Xfinity
fleets.notes: Comcast xfinitywifi hotspot or Xfinity / XFSETUP gateway name. Most boxes are Arris / Hitron / Technicolor OEM — those hit the OEM row.

fleets.name: Yuneec
fleets.notes: Yuneec drone. The name starts with Yuneec. A renamed network misses. Often no Remote ID plate.

fleets.name: Zyxel
fleets.notes: Zyxel home or SMB gateway / access point.
